Euler transformation produces the analytic numerator Qθ,b(ζ)={}_2F_1(−θ,−b;1−b;ζ) and nonvanishing remaining factors. Its nth n≥1 coefficient is b/(n−b)(−1)^(n+1) binom(θ,n)>0. The reflection/Beta formula and 1/(n−b) integral give finite positive pushforward ν with Q=1+∫ζ/(1−tζ)dν; Im Q has sign Im ζ, so no nonreal zeros. Real-positive Q>1; on (−1,0), Q′>0 so at most one simple negative root. Q(−1)=1−Lθ(b) with L strictly increasing continuously from 0 to infinity, since b u^(−b) increases and total mass diverges as b→1. This yields a unique b*, no interior zero at equality, exactly one above, and the implicit derivative shows transverse crossing and monotone root toward zero.
